q: Flor's seasonal rhythm and the cellar factors that feed it:
accept: spring autumn blooms humidity temperature albariza sand floors
levante poniente winds humidity 15 percent
ans: Blooms spring and autumn; thrives on humidity (sand floors watered), mild temperatures, 14.5–15.5% alcohol, and airflow from the poniente wind
exp: Sanlúcar's sea humidity = thickest flor = Manzanilla's salinity.

q: How often is Vintage Port declared, when in the wine's life is the decision taken, and who must approve it?
accept: three per decade second spring ivdp approval
about three a decade decided in the second spring
three per decade 2016 2017 consecutive
ans: Roughly three declarations a decade. Each house decides independently in the second spring after the harvest — around the wine's eighteenth month, before bottling — and the wine must be submitted to the IVDP for approval; 2016 and 2017 were the rare consecutive declarations
exp: 'Declaration' is each house's call in the second spring.

q: Explain how to assess a Sherry's age and style blind.
accept: flor character salinity versus oxidative nuttiness color depth viscosity
flor versus oxidation then colour
ans: First ask flor or not — bread dough and salinity versus walnut and toffee. Then read colour depth and viscosity for age, and sweetness last
exp: Palomino's neutrality means everything you taste came from the cellar.

q: Describe how a criadera-and-solera system is actually run, and explain what fractional blending achieves.
accept: scales of butts drawn from the solera and refilled from the criadera above
the saca from the solera and the rocio from the criadera with nothing ever emptied
fractional blending averages vintages and leaves a trace of old wine in every bottle
criaderas numbered outward feed the solera which is the scale that gets bottled
ans: The butts are arranged in scales of age. The solera is the oldest scale, named from suelo, the floor, and the criaderas or nurseries are numbered outward from it — the first criadera feeds the solera, the second feeds the first, and so on up to the youngest, which is refreshed from sobretablas. Bottling draws only from the solera: the saca, in practice a quarter to a third of each butt, never the whole thing. Each scale is then topped up from the one above it, the rocio, poured gently down the wall of the butt so the flor blanket is not broken, and a butt is deliberately left about five-sixths full to give the flor air. What this buys is threefold. Consistency, because vintage variation and flor's seasonal blooms and die-backs are averaged out. Continuity, because nothing is ever emptied, so a trace of very old wine survives in every bottling and the average age climbs to an equilibrium set by how much is drawn each year. And refreshment, because the young wine carries nutrients and alcohol that keep the flor alive in a way a static cask could not. VOS and VORS certify average ages of twenty and thirty years.
exp: Candidates routinely invert this, calling the youngest scale the solera. Fix it with the etymology: solera is the floor, so it is the row on the ground, and it is the oldest. The refreshment point is the one that separates a good answer from a recited one — a flor solera is not merely a blending device, it is a life-support system for a yeast film, which is why the same architecture is optional for oxidative Oloroso and essential for Fino and Manzanilla.

q: Explain albariza and name the pagos a candidate should know.
accept: the chalky white marl that holds winter rain with pagos like macharnudo carrascal and balbaina
albariza is chalk that stores water and the pagos include macharnudo and miraflores
calcium carbonate marl of the jerez hills with balbaina anina and carrascal
white chalky soil that crusts to hold moisture pagos macharnudo balbaina
ans: Albariza is the brilliant white, chalky marl of the Jerez hills — marine sediment of the Oligocene and Miocene, laid down with diatom skeletons, running roughly 25 to 40% calcium carbonate. Its behaviour is what matters: it soaks up the winter rain, then bakes into a hard reflective crust in the heat that seals the moisture beneath, so a vine can draw on stored water through a rainless summer of nearly 300 sunshine days. Aserpia, the old practice of trenching square basins between the rows, existed to catch that rain before it ran off. Palomino on albariza gives finer, more delicate wine than on the barros clays or the arenas sands of the flats, which is why the classification of pagos matters. The names to have are Macharnudo, Carrascal, Anina and Balbaina around Jerez, Miraflores and Martin Miguel in Sanlucar, and Los Tercios and Balbaina Baja toward El Puerto. Valdespino's Inocente from Macharnudo Alto is the proof that a single pago speaks.
exp: Sherry is normally taught as a cellar wine, and this question checks whether the candidate can also talk about the vineyard. The 2022 reform gave that new weight by formalising single-vineyard and pago mentions on the label, so the old assumption that Palomino is a blank slate and everything happens in the bodega is being actively dismantled by producers like Equipo Navazos, Willy Perez and Ramiro Ibanez. Know the soil types in order of quality — albariza, then barros, then arenas — and the sub-types tosca cerrada, barajuelas and lentejuelas if pressed.

q: Port's fermentation is cut short. Explain what that forces on the winemaking, and describe the modern answers to it.
accept: only 36 to 48 hours to extract so foot treading and robotic lagares are needed
half the sugar remains at fortification so extraction must be fast and violent
lagares treading autovinifiers and robotic lagares do the extraction in two days
fortified at about six or seven percent alcohol with 77 percent aguardente
ans: Fortification happens when roughly half the sugar is still unfermented, at about six to seven degrees of alcohol, often within two days of the crush. That leaves only about 36 to 48 hours to take all the colour and tannin a wine destined for fifty years in bottle will ever have — where a dry red might macerate for two or three weeks. So extraction has to be violent and total in the time available, and it has to happen while the ferment is still sugary and the alcohol low, which is a poor solvent for phenolics. The classic answer is foot treading in shallow granite lagares: the disciplined corte, a linked line of treaders working the mass for two hours, then liberdade, and the human foot turns out to be near-perfect because it crushes skins without shredding seeds. The modern answers replicate the same work — the Ducellier autovinifier using fermentation gas pressure to drive its own pumping over, piston-driven robotic lagares introduced by the Symingtons in the late 1990s, and intensive pump-over and pistonage regimes. Then the aguardente goes in at 77%, about a fifth of the final volume, killing the yeast and locking the residual sugar in place.
exp: The examiner wants cause and effect, not a description of treading as folklore. Two facts anchor everything else: the ferment is stopped at half sugar, and the extraction window is under two days. Everything from lagar design to robotic pistons follows from that constraint. Contrast the mutage spirits deliberately — 77% aguardente for Port carries some flavour of its own and is added in quantity, while a vin doux naturel takes 96% neutral spirit precisely so the spirit says nothing.

q: Explain the AP number (Amtliche Prüfungsnummer) and what a somm can read from it.
accept: official testing number last digits year of application lot
ap nummer bottling lot and year
ans: The official quality-test number: encoded testing station, estate, lot, and — crucially — the year of application (last digits), distinguishing multiple bottlings of one Prädikat
exp: How collectors tell two different Auslesen of the same vineyard apart.

q: What is a 'Grosslage' versus an 'Einzellage', with the classic misleading example?
accept: collective site versus single vineyard piesporter michelsberg
michelsberg grosslage badstube einzellage
ans: Einzellage = single vineyard; Grosslage = large collective zone. 'Piesporter Michelsberg' (Grosslage) misleads buyers seeking Piesporter Goldtröpfchen (Einzellage)
